question: What will Serbia's year-on-year consumer price inflation be in October 2026?

calls.reasoning: October y/y ≈ Sept 4.1% + (Oct-2026 m/m − Oct-2025 m/m of +0.5%). The large margin-cap base effect was in Sept 2025 (−1.6% m/m), so October has no comparable base shock. Fuel prices were frozen at 236/207 RSD through all of October 2026 (no transport push). NBS (8 Oct 2026) expects inflation 'around 4%' from September with upside risks. Its May report expected a temporary move above 4.5% around end-2026. Upside: administered-price increases and food normalization after the margin cap expired in March 2026. Downside: soft seasonal food prices. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- RZS Sept 2026 CPI: +4.1% y/y (Aug 2.2%, Jul 1.9%), +0.2% m/m. Food y/y about −1.3% (TradingEconomics) or −1.8% (background), up from −6.3% in Aug. Transport +10.1% y/y. (tradingeconomics, Oct 2026)
- Oct 2025: +0.5% m/m and 2.8% y/y (Sept 2025 2.9%). Sept 2025 was −1.6% m/m after the retail margin cap decree took effect on 1 Sep 2025. Aug 2025 was 4.7% y/y. (tradingeconomics news)
- Arithmetic: Oct 2026 y/y ≈ 4.1 + (Oct 2026 m/m − 0.5).
- Margin cap decree (20% cap on food, household chemicals and personal care) ran 1 Sep 2025 to 1 Mar 2026. Amended 30 Jan 2026. No extension found. (BDK Advokati)
- NBS on 8 Oct 2026: key rate held at 5.75%. Expects inflation around 4% from September, with elevated risks from a longer energy crisis and higher primary commodity prices. (Bloomberg Adria)
- NBS May 2026 report: expected inflation temporarily slightly above 4.5% at end-2026 and early 2027, from the low Sept 2025 base plus energy, then back in the band by mid-2027. The Aug 2026 revision cut average 2026 inflation to about 3.2%. (Nova Ekonomija; naslovi.net)
- Fuel: capped retail prices of diesel 236 and petrol 207 RSD were unchanged from early Sept through end-Oct 2026. Excise cut of 25% and fuel export ban extended. (B92, 30 Oct 2026)
- Sept 2026 administered and service items: water +21.8% y/y, rents +10.6%, wastewater +12.9%. (srpske.rs, per background)
- TradingEconomics model: 3.5% by end of Q4 2026.
- NBS target 3% ± 1.5% (band ceiling 4.5%).
- Status quo: annual rate near the September level unless the October m/m differs from last October's +0.5%.
- Resolves off the first RZS CN11 release for October 2026 (expected 12 Nov 2026), annual rate in %, not later revisions.
- Event window: single monthly print for October 2026; the reference month has ended and data are not yet published (as of 2 Nov 2026).
- Searched but not found: any October 2026 flash estimate or analyst preview; electricity price changes in Oct 2025 or Oct 2026; detail on October 2025 food m/m; any prediction market (none found).
calls.reference_class: Month-to-month change in Serbia's headline y/y CPI from September to October in non-shock years (e.g., 2024 4.2->4.3, 2025 2.9->2.8), i.e. annual rate persistence when the base-month m/m is ordinary

calls.reasoning: Oct y/y ≈ Sep 4.1% + (Oct-2026 m/m − Oct-2025 m/m of +0.5%). Oct-2025 m/m included a 6.6% household electricity hike (1 Oct 2025, ~0.3pp of CPI); the 2026 hike was postponed past the 25 Oct election (Danas, Aug 31 2026), so the base effect subtracts ~0.3pp. Fuel flat through October 2026; margin-cap decree expired Mar 2026 so no extra food base effect in Oct. Services and housing costs remain strong and the NBS guides 'around 4%'. Expected Oct-2026 m/m 0.2-0.5 → y/y ~3.8-4.1; median 3.9. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold none per harness; none found in my searches).
calls.dossier:
- RZS Sep 2026 CPI: 4.1% y/y (Aug 2.2%), +0.2% m/m, +3.3% vs Dec 2025; food -1.8% y/y (Aug -7.2%); water +21.8%, rents +10.6%, transport +1.2% m/m, recreation/culture -5.6% m/m (srpske.rs, 12 Oct 2026; tradingeconomics).
- Oct 2025 base: y/y 2.8% (Sep 2025 2.9%), m/m +0.5% (tradingeconomics/longbridge Nov 2025 release coverage).
- Household regulated electricity rose 6.6% on 1 Oct 2025 (AERS via seenews; Serbian Monitor Jul 2025). Electricity weight in CPI roughly ~5% (estimate, not verified for ECOICOP v2 2025 basket).
- 2026 electricity hike (IMF commitment: by 1 Oct 2026, ≥ CPI+1pp, est. 3.7-4.7%) was NOT submitted by Aug 31; postponed until after elections, formal deadline end-2026 (Danas 31 Aug 2026; Clavis 18 Sep 2026). No evidence found of an Oct 1 2026 hike.
- Retail margin cap decree in force 1 Sep 2025 – expired 1 Mar 2026, not extended (Cekos; 021.rs). Its base effect mainly hit Sep 2026 print.
- Fuel: max retail diesel 236 RSD, BMB95 207 RSD, unchanged for several weeks through 23 Oct 2026, diesel at record (danubeogradu.rs).
- NBS (8 Oct 2026, rate held 5.75%): y/y inflation expected around 4% from September and through 2027; drivers low base from margin decree plus global energy prices. Next NBS meeting 12 Nov.
- Agricultural producer prices -8.7% y/y in August 2026, fruit -23.3% (srpske.rs).
- Arithmetic identity: Oct y/y ≈ 4.1 + (Oct-2026 m/m − 0.5). Electricity base effect alone ≈ −0.3pp if no Oct 2026 hike.
- Status quo: September's 4.1%. Event window: single October 2026 CPI print, released ~12 Nov 2026; as of 2 Nov the reference month is complete, data unpublished.
- Resolves off RZS first-published Oct 2026 annual rate (CN11), not HICP or later revisions.
- Searched but not found: Oct 2026 flash/analyst consensus, gas price change in Oct 2026, food price data for Oct 2026, any prediction market (none found).
calls.reference_class: Serbian CPI one-month-ahead y/y changes computed via base-effect arithmetic (prior y/y + current m/m − year-ago m/m), 2024-2026

No electricity hike in Oct 2026 (EPS failed to file in time); fuel prices flat at 236/207 RSD since late Sept. Seasonal food/clothing and ongoing service/admin increases suggest Oct-2026 m/m ~+0.3%, so y/y slips from 4.1% to ~3.9-4.0%. NBS guided ~4% from September; upside risks from the energy shock and food momentum (+0.6% m/m in Sept). No prediction market found.

calls.reasoning: Oct y/y ≈ 4.1 + (Oct-2026 m/m − 0.5). The Oct-2025 base includes a 6.6% household electricity hike (~0.3pp); no Oct-2026 hike (postponed past the election). Fuel was frozen all October. Seasonal food/clothing plus ongoing admin/service increases → Oct-2026 m/m ~0.3-0.4, so y/y ~3.9-4.0. NBS guides 'around 4%'. Food momentum and rounding of 4.1 tilt slightly up versus Runs 2/3. No prediction market found.
calls.reconciliation: Main dispute: whether the Oct-2025 base m/m (+0.5) contains a one-off electricity hike absent in Oct 2026. Runs 2 and 3 independently report the AERS-approved 6.6% hike on 1 Oct 2025 and the postponement of the 2026 hike. Run 1 did not examine this, so its 4.1 median ignores a ~0.3pp negative base effect. I accept the Runs 2/3 factual reading. Remaining judgment: underlying Oct-2026 m/m ex-electricity. Placed at 0.3-0.4 given food momentum and admin-price creep, giving a median of 3.95. No web access this run.
